turns.t: Hello, Josh? I'm Maria, I'm the nurse from school. Your mum's on the phone, she said it's fine for you to be seen without her. ~
Okay. ~
Hello Josh, I'm Dr Hayes. How old are you? ~
Twelve. ~
Maria says you've been getting tummy cramps at school. Tell me about them.
They come after lunch. It's like a squeezing, and sometimes I have to run to the toilet.
How often?
Most days this week. Not every day before that.
His mum says it's been about a month, on and off. ~
Do you feel sick, or have you been sick?
No. Not sick.
Any blood when you go to the toilet?
No.
What do you eat for lunch? ~
School dinners. Pasta, mostly. And a flapjack. ~
Any milk or cheese? ~
Milk with my cereal. And yoghurt. ~
Do the cramps happen at the weekend? ~
Not really. Only school days. ~
He's been moved up a class this term, and there's a big test coming. ~
Is school okay, Josh? Is there anything worrying you? ~
A bit. The tests. And there's a boy who's mean. ~
Thank you for telling me. That sounds hard. Does anything else bother you, aching, headaches? ~
Sometimes headaches. ~
What medicines do you take, Maria's notes say?
His mum says, an inhaler, salbutamol, as needed, for asthma, and a vitamin, Vitamin D, 400 units, once a day.
Let me check his pulse and temperature. ~
Okay. ~
Pulse 84, temperature 36.6, and his weight is 38 kilos.
That's the same as last term, doctor. ~
Good. Lie back, Josh. I'll press your tummy. Tell me if it hurts.
It tickles. ~
His tummy is soft and not tender.
Is it something serious? ~
Nothing here worries me. Tummy ache linked to school days is very common, and often related to worry. I'd like to see how it goes, and I don't want to label it yet. ~
Will I have to take medicine? ~
No medicine, Josh. I'd like you to try a few things. Eat lunch slowly, drink water, and go to the toilet before the tests, not after.
Okay. ~
I'll keep an eye on him, and I'll talk to his teacher about the boy. ~
Thank you, Maria. I'd like to see Josh again in three weeks, with his mum, and we'll talk it through.
I'll arrange that. ~

chief_complaint.value: you've been getting tummy cramps at school

physical_examination.finding: tummy is soft and not tender

clinical_actions.description: Eat lunch slowly, drink water and use the toilet before tests
